questions.prompt: Why does fn f(x: &str) -> &str compile without writing explicit lifetime annotations?

options.a: Lifetimes are optional in Rust functions
options.b: Lifetime elision: with one input reference, the compiler assumes the output borrows from it

questions.prompt: Why can NO lifetime annotation ever make returning a reference to a local variable (return &local;) legal in Rust?

options.a: It is restricted by a style lint
options.b: The local variable is destroyed when the stack frame returns — lifetime annotations describe relationships, they cannot extend runtime memory
options.c: It is legal only when using &'static

questions.prompt: The standard escape from E0515: return an ___ value (String, Vec, …) instead of a reference.
